author: reek
body: fetch, post and resolve-dns are definitions in Net chapter HttpFetch. They were effect operations that nothing implemented: a call type-checked clean and died at the end of emit with CDX2040. That failure was invisible to the battery, because no test called one. This one does -- resolve-dns on a dotted quad takes the fast path and never touches the wire, so it runs headless, and it still has to link. If the implementation is ever removed the call stops resolving and this test stops compiling, which is the point.

author: reek
body: The rest is known-answer: the URL parse, the header framing, and the declared content length. The length is what tells a complete body from a truncated one, so it is worth pinning to a fixture.

author: reek
body: The live half -- a real GET and POST against a real server, and a name resolved on the wire -- cannot run here, because the battery starts no server. It is exercised by hand.

author: reek
body: A response as it arrives off the wire: ASCII, CRLF-delimited, with a declared length. CR and LF are written as their wire codes because a Codex string literal has no escape for them.

author: reek
body: fetch, post and resolve-dns answer with a Result, so a failure is a value the caller can see rather than an empty string it cannot tell from an empty body. Both directions are printed here.
